rationale: Override. The AI stopped at needs_more_info because it could not prove the app was illegitimate. The app catalog settles it. Harborline's real e-signature vendor is Northwind eSign, app 4c1e7a52-0b9d-4f3e-8a61-2d5f9e0b7c13, verified publisher, admin-consented by IT, approved for User.Read and Files.Read only. The consented app has a different app ID, a name built to look like the sanctioned one, and asks for Mail.ReadWrite plus offline_access through user consent. A real Northwind add-in would not need Ada to consent at all, and would not need to write to her mailbox. That is an illicit consent grant: a refresh token with read and write on a CUI-handling mailbox that survives a password reset. Waiting for more information leaves that token live.

ai_actions.reason: Find the lure. Whatever sent her the consent link likely went to others.

ai_actions.target: e93b5c1d-7a40-4d2f-b8e6-0c3a91f5d274 (service principal 5f0d2a8c-91b3-4e67-a4d1-7c2e8b9f3a60), delegated grant for ada.marsh@harborline.example
ai_actions.reason: Cut the app's access to her mailbox now.
Invalidate refresh tokens issued under the grant.

added_actions.reason: Disable and delete the service principal so no other user can consent to it. Removing one user's grant leaves the app available to the next click.

tuning_notes: Enrichment looks apps up by exact ID only, so a lookalike scores the same as any unknown app. Add a display-name similarity check against sanctioned apps and flag a near match with a different app ID. That single field is what moved this case from 'unknown' to 'malicious'.
Turn off user consent for apps from unverified publishers in Entra. The detection is the backstop, not the control.
